We are seeking a qualified capital/finance professional to lead the capital and control workstream for new regulated insurance entities established by the Group — including DFSA, Cayman and Lloyd’s structures. The primary focus of the role is on new entity establishment: defining the capital structure, building the financial control framework, and establishing the regulatory reporting infrastructure from inception. Once entities are operational, you will support their ongoing financial and regulatory requirements as needed, alongside supporting existing entities and reinsurance programmes where required. You will also supervise a junior analyst. This is a build‑focused role for someone comfortable standing things up from scratch, not just running steady‑state reporting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the financial establishment of new regulated entities (DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s and others) – defining the opening balance sheet, capital structure and financial control framework from inception, and ensuring each entity is correctly capitalised and controlled before it writes business.
  • Build capital adequacy and solvency models for each new entity to meet regulator requirements; maintain and update these models as the entity grows.
  • Establish the regulatory reporting framework for each new jurisdiction (e.g., DFSA, Cayman, Lloyd’s), including designing the reporting pack, setting the reporting calendar and producing the first returns; hand over to ongoing support once embedded.
  • Build the financial model for each new entity – three‑statement model and entity‑level profit and loss – establishing the management reporting suite from which ongoing reporting will run.
  • Establish the reinsurance programme accounting structure for new entities (quota share, excess of loss, ceding commission), ensuring the accounting treatment and control framework are correctly set up from inception; support existing programmes as required.
  • Produce the first monthly management accounts and entity‑level reporting pack for each new entity, establishing the format, commentary structure and distribution; support the ongoing production of these for existing entities as required.
  • Reconcile intercompany balances and positions across group entities.
  • Manage the Group’s Funds at Lloyd’s (FAL) position for the Syndicate in a Box (SIAB) – providing feeds to C&C’s selected managing agent for the annual capital setting process (ECM/SBF cycle), optimising FAL composition across cash, LOCs and approved investments, responding to Lloyd’s capital calls, and maintaining the FAL headroom analysis relative to the approved capital requirement.
  • Run capital adequacy stress testing and scenario analysis across the Group’s regulated entities – including shock loss, premium volume growth and FX sensitivity – to assess headroom above SCR/MCR thresholds and inform capital deployment decisions.
  • Manage collateral arrangements supporting the Group’s reinsurance programmes – including letters of credit, trust accounts and cash deposits – ensuring collateral is correctly sized, documented and renewed in line with programme terms and regulatory requirements.
  • Own the capital waterfall and inter‑entity funding mechanics – managing dividend upstream, shareholder loan repayment and capital repatriation between regulated entities and the parent, and ensuring all movements are within approved limits and correctly documented.
  • Track and report reinsurance counterparty credit exposure across the Group’s programmes, maintaining the counterparty register and flagging rating changes, concentration risk or collateral shortfalls.
  • Produce the board‑level capital reporting pack – including capital dashboard, solvency headroom by entity, FAL position and stress test outcomes – on a quarterly basis or as required by the board or managing agent.
  • Support existing entities and reinsurance programmes as required, including covering financial control, reporting or capital queries where capacity or expertise is needed.
  • Supervise and direct the Capital & Structuring Analyst on day‑to‑day work.

Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Android AOSP Hardware Enablement Engineer to bring up and enable automotive hardware platforms for Android Open Source Project (AOSP) and Android Automotive OS (AAOS) builds.

The engineer will be responsible for enabling the underlying hardware and software stack required to build, boot, and operate Android on an automotive SoC platform. This includes bootloader configuration, Linux kernel integration, device tree development, vendor BSP integration, hardware driver enablement, Android build configuration, and debugging of hardware‑related boot and runtime issues.

The candidate will work closely with SoC vendors, hardware teams, BSP developers, kernel engineers, and Android framework teams to deliver a stable and functional Android infotainment platform.

Key Responsibilities

AOSP Build System and Platform Integration

  • Set up and maintain AOSP source code and development environments.
  • Configure and execute Android platform builds using Soong, Android.bp, Make, and related build tools.
  • Integrate vendor‑provided Android BSP packages into the AOSP source tree.
  • Configure product definitions, device configurations, board configurations, and vendor‑specific build components.
  • Develop and maintain device‑specific build configurations, including device/, vendor/, and relevant kernel integration components.
  • Configure product makefiles, product packages, build variants, and system/vendor partition requirements.
  • Resolve build failures, dependency issues, missing modules, and compilation errors.
  • Maintain build scripts and documentation for repeatable platform builds.

Bootloader and Platform Bring‑Up

  • Enable the Android boot process on new or existing automotive hardware platforms.
  • Work with bootloaders such as U‑Boot or vendor‑specific implementations based on the target SoC.
  • Configure boot arguments, boot targets, image loading, memory reservations, and device tree handoff.
  • Coordinate with SoC vendors to resolve platform‑specific boot and firmware issues.

Linux Kernel and Device Tree Enablement

  • Integrate and configure vendor Linux kernels compatible with the selected Android release.
  • Enable required kernel configurations and device drivers for the target hardware.
  • Develop, modify, and debug Device Tree Source (DTS/DTSI) files and overlays.
  • Configure hardware resources such as GPIOs, clocks, regulators, interrupts, IOMMU, DMA, and memory regions.
  • Integrate vendor kernel modules and troubleshoot module loading or dependency issues.

Hardware Driver and Peripheral Enablement

Enable and validate the hardware peripherals required for an automotive infotainment system, including: - Display interfaces: MIPI DSI, eDP, LVDS, HDMI - Touchscreen controllers and input devices - Audio codecs, I²S/TDM interfaces, amplifiers, audio routing - USB host/device controllers, storage, peripheral connectivity - Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, GNSS, Ethernet - Camera interfaces and sensor connectivity (where applicable) - I²C, SPI, UART, GPIO, PCIe, and other SoC peripherals - Automotive CAN interfaces and related transceivers (where supported) - Power management ICs, thermal sensors, watchdogs, suspend/resume functionality

Hardware Debugging and System Validation

  • Debug the complete boot flow from bootloader to Android launcher.
  • Analyze bootloader logs, kernel dmesg, Android Logcat, tombstones, and service startup logs.
  • Use ADB, fastboot, serial consoles, JTAG, and hardware debugging tools as available.

Automotive Platform Integration

  • Enable and validate Android Automotive OS on automotive infotainment reference boards and target hardware.
  • Work with automotive SoC platforms and vendor BSPs from suppliers such as Qualcomm, NXP, or MediaTek.
  • Coordinate with hardware design, BSP, firmware, Android framework, and application teams.
  • Support hardware variants, board revisions, and product‑specific configurations.
  • Assist with Android compatibility testing and platform validation requirements.
  • Support integration of automotive features such as vehicle properties, audio, display, connectivity, and power‑state management.
  • Follow applicable automotive development, security, and software quality requirements.
summary: Experienced Android AOSP Hardware Enablement Engineer needed to bring up automotive platforms, handling bootloader, kernel, and driver integration. Role involves cross‑team collaboration for stable infotainment.
